headline: Arizona State's Clutch Defense Holds as Alabama's Prolific Air Attack Falls Short
body: Arizona State escaped Tuscaloosa with a 34-28 victory despite being outgained 400 to 359 total yards, a stark reversal that came down to possession management and Alabama's self-inflicted wounds. The visitors turned the ball over twice—both fumbles—while Alabama's offense never surrendered possession, yet the Sun Devils' defense tightened when it mattered most. Alabama's aerial assault was undeniable: Cortez completed 19 of 34 for 331 yards with two touchdowns, and Monroe's 67 receiving yards kept chains moving, but Arizona State's pass rush generated enough pressure to prevent the Crimson Tide from finding the endzone in critical moments.

Thomas piloted Arizona State's offense with surgical precision rather than volume, going 21 of 35 for 248 yards and three touchdowns. The key differential emerged in how Arizona State controlled the line of scrimmage on the ground: despite modest yardage, the Sun Devils' commitment to running the football—121 yards on the day—forced Alabama's defense to defend the entire field and shortened the Crimson Tide's scoring opportunities. Perry's six receptions and one touchdown catch exemplified Arizona State's balanced attack; the Sun Devils weren't winning a shootout, so they didn't try to.

Keith Adams Jr. torched Arizona State for 55 rushing yards on 12 carries and punched in two touchdowns, earning Player of the Game honors and proving Alabama could move the football on the ground when given opportunity. Yet Arizona State's defense, anchored by Wyatt's five tackles and crucial sack, refused to break late. The moment came midway through the fourth quarter when Arizona State forced an Alabama fumble in the red zone—the second turnover of the evening—and the Sun Devils converted field position into a touchdown that proved the difference.
turningPoint: Arizona State's second forced fumble, a red-zone turnover midway through the fourth quarter, shifted momentum decisively in the Sun Devils' favor after Alabama had controlled possession and yardage for much of the game.

unsungHero.name: Wyatt
unsungHero.why: His sack and five tackles were quiet anchors on Arizona State's defense, forcing uncomfortable decisions on Cortez and collapsing Alabama's timing without the highlight nature of Adams Jr.'s two rushing touchdowns that dominated the offensive narrative.
